subject: Nanotechnology
title: Photocatalytic Hydrogen
description: A fast breakdown of Photocatalytic Hydrogen for builders.

hook.text: Sunlight plus water plus a nano catalyst equals hydrogen — solar fuel with no electricity needed.

buildup.text: Semiconductor nanoparticles absorb light and generate electron-hole pairs that drive water-splitting reactions.

discovery.text: TiO₂ nanoparticles were the first photocatalysts — but only absorb UV light, just 4% of the solar spectrum.

twist.text: Visible-light photocatalysts like g-C₃N₄ absorb more spectrum but recombine charges too fast — low efficiency.

climax.text: Z-scheme heterostructures mimic photosynthesis — two nano catalysts working in tandem boost efficiency tenfold.

punchline.text: Sunlight on a nano particle splits water into fuel — artificial photosynthesis.

quiz.question: Why is TiO₂ limited as a solar photocatalyst?
options: It dissolves in water during the reaction
It only absorbs ultraviolet light, which is just 4% of the solar spectrum
It produces oxygen instead of hydrogen
